title: Operational readiness & release note ownership + rollback playbook for runtime-1.20
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Coordinate cross-functional readiness for the runtime-1.20 public rollout. This ticket consolidates release-note ownership, preflight cutoffs, a minimal rollback playbook, and incident communication templates. Scope includes hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deploy paths; exclude feature flags unrelated to core serving runtime changes.

Goals:
- Ensure a single source of truth for release notes and 'what changed' messaging across docs, SDK repos, and marketplace listings.
- Validate canary and rollout metrics, dashboards, and SLO guardrails are in place before any traffic ramp.
- Document a concise, testable rollback plan that SREs and Engineering can execute within the SLA window.
- Provide ready-to-send incident templates for on-call and comms teams to use if we hit customer-facing regressions.

Key stakeholders and owners:
- PM owner: Liam Chen (this ticket)
- Engineering owner: Priya Rao (ENG-2041)
- SRE/Oncall lead: Mateo Alvarez (ENG-2150)
- DevRel/Docs owner (release notes): Sara Kim
- Sales & GTM briefing: Javier Ordonez
- Legal & Security: Elena Novak
- Support playbook owner: Nora Briggs

Out-of-band artifacts:
- Release notes draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime-1.20/release-notes-draft
- Rollback runbook (living): https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/runtime-rollback
- Canary dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-1.20-canary
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls?q=is%3Apr+milestone%3Aruntime-1.20

Acceptance criteria (must pass before broad traffic ramp):
- Release notes owner has finalized user-facing copy and SDK changelogs, and copy reviewed by legal.
- Canary window (24h) shows no regression in 99p latency, token rate, or error rate above threshold.
- Observability: per-route token-level traces and error alerts are green and firing correctly.
- Rollback playbook validated in canary dry-run (simulated rollbacks during low-traffic window).
- Support has prepared canned responses and escalation steps for top 5 user-facing issues.

Delivery constraints and non-go conditions:
- Do not begin >50% customer ramp if SLO alerts fire or rollback automation tests fail.
- Hold if any critical security review items remain OPEN.
rollback_playbook_summary: 1) Immediate containment: flip public routing to previous pinned model-version (runtime-1.19) using routing policy 'pin-previous' and reduce canary weight to 0%. 2) If API schema compatible, perform automated KV cache invalidation for affected pools to prevent stale state. 3) If rollback to previous model fails, fail-over to 'fallback-compat' binary that serves a narrower feature set. 4) Post-rollback: collect shard-level logs, export last-10m token traces and create an incident in PagerDuty with priority P0. 5) Postmortem: 48h triage meeting, 7-day RCA mailing, attach updated runbook. Links: confluence runbook above.
canary_policy: Phase 1 (internal): 0.5% traffic for 2h across US region. Phase 2 (external canary): 2% traffic for 24h across US+EU. Phase 3 (ramp): incremental increases 5%/6h if no regressions until target capacity. Automatic rollback triggers: 3x increase in 5xxs over baseline, 15% degradation in 99p latency, token-cost spike >25% unusual. Manual 'hold' option retained by SRE/PM.
incident_comm_template:
Subject: [INCIDENT][runtime-1.20] Brief summary of impact

What happened: short bullet describing observed problem and affected endpoints
When it started: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
Impact: customers affected, degraded latencies, failed requests %
Mitigation in progress: actions we are taking now (canary rollback, capacity increase, circuiting features)
Next update cadence: every 15 minutes until resolved
Contact: on-call SRE (pager), PM owner: Liam Chen, comms lead: Nora Briggs
Postmortem plan: 48h initial sync, full RCA within 7 days

Template for public status page: "We are currently investigating elevated error rates impacting the /v1/generate endpoint. We have deployed mitigations and are monitoring."
release_notes_tldr: runtime-1.20 improves batching heuristics, introduces kernel-level attention optimization for long contexts, and updates model variant selection policies. Known risk: subtle tokenization edge-case on a small subset of older model checkpoints; mitigations in place and guided rollback plan available.
acceptance_criteria: Rollback dry-run executed with telemetry captured
Support replies and canned messages validated

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tokenization edge-case on older model checkpoints -> Mitigation: preflight checksum validation and opt-out list for pinned customers
Risk: Unexpected latency spike under wide contexts -> Mitigation: limit max_context on canary, enable aggressive batching under degraded mode
Risk: Release notes mismatch across channels -> Mitigation: single canonical release notes doc and script to sync SDK changelogs
